name: Burlcowl
description: Feet set apart and the club held across the chest, the braced frame takes a shove without giving ground.

name: Straight Belabor
description: Both hands lift the club past the ear and drop it onto the target's shoulder or crown.

name: Single Bellyswell
description: A short low swing raps the club across the shin of an advancing opponent.

name: Solid Handholdgrip
description: The club's shaft knocks an incoming arm or weapon aside before the swing comes home.

name: Swaying Roundhead
description: Small sliding steps close the gap without crossing the feet or lifting the club's head.

name: Wallopblow
description: After a missed blow the club's momentum is turned and thumped back against the ribs.

name: Raised Girth
description: Hands spaced on the stick and elbows tucked, it is raised as a bar that stops blows to the head.

name: Hard Clout
description: A flat horizontal swing at waist height lands the stick across the ribs and side.

name: Nabbing Thickend
description: A sharp downward tap on the opponent's wrist loosens the grip on a weapon.

name: Stepping Heartwood
description: Heels light and weight low, the student retreats in even paces while keeping the stick forward.

name: Level Thump
description: The stick falls from shoulder height onto the front of the knee, slowing the advance.

name: Raised Bulge
description: The knobbed end points at the opponent's face, and the stance holds him at arm's length.

name: Girthhit
description: A straight shove of the knob drives into the breastbone and knocks the breath short.

name: Catching Cudgel
description: The knob catches behind an ankle or elbow and a sharp pull breaks the opponent's balance.

name: Cudgelhit
description: From low at the hip, the knob swings upward into the underside of the forearm or jaw.

name: Stouthusk
description: The thick knob meets the incoming blow and turns it off along the angle of the shaft.

name: Swaying Burl
description: A lateral glide leaves the line of the attack while the cudgel stays raised and ready.

name: Quick Wallop
description: A wide looping arc brings the knob down onto the collarbone from the side.

name: Snug Knob
description: Squared in a narrow stance with the club vertical, the watchman fills a doorway or lane.

name: Bulgehusk
description: Both hands hold the club crosswise and lean it into a crowd to push it back.

name: Firm Bellyswell
description: A short chop lands on the outer thigh and numbs the leg of a fleeing offender.

name: Knobwedge
description: A wide swing passing just short of the face makes an aggressor flinch and halt.

name: Solid Burl
description: Pinning the club's butt to the elbow, the watchman redirects a thrown punch past the shoulder.

name: Sideways Wallop
description: An even gliding stride advances along a street while keeping the club level and the balance low.

name: Planted Stout
description: The cudgel hangs low against the thigh and rises to a diagonal block when threatened.

name: Blunt Girth
description: Pulled from the belt in a single arc, the cudgel swings flat into the opponent's flank.

name: Knobhusk
description: The sliding palm shifts the grip up the shaft so a blow glances off the wood.

name: Short Bludgeon
description: A downward flick of the cudgel lands on the ankle bone of the lead foot.

name: Belabor Skitter
description: Two quick backward paces break contact while the cudgel keeps the pursuer at its length.

name: Settled Handholdgrip
description: A thread of qi settles in the palms and forearms, firming the grip and bracing against heavy blows.

name: Upward Clout
description: On the out-breath the bludgeon drops and thuds into the target with the whole body behind it.

name: Wallopbump
description: A short chopping blow lands on the point of the shoulder and deadens the arm below it.

name: Short Thump
description: A compact flick of the wrist and qi cracks the bludgeon sharply into a hand or elbow.

name: Hitching Bulge
description: The free hand seizes the collar and drags the opponent into the path of the swing.

name: Holding Stout
description: Rolling the shaft over the wrist, the bludgeon carries a blow away along the grain.

name: Shifting Knob
description: A quick lateral step slips the thrust, and a rap to the exposed hand follows at once.

name: Stiff Heartwood
description: A small qi-backed tap on the wrist nerve leaves the opponent's fingers slack for a breath.

name: Thickend Lid
description: The heavy oaken club is held upright, and its mass stops light blows without strain.

name: Clouthit
description: The dense core of the oak falls straight down, with qi settling into the wood at impact.

name: Quick Roundhead
description: A sloping downward blow rings off the collarbone and drops the opponent's guard arm.

name: Stoutpause
description: As the opponent presses in, the haft is driven into his chest and he is thrown off his line.

name: Light Burl
description: Qi settled in the soles lets the student slide across the ground without losing weight.

name: Blunt Handholdgrip
description: The club bounces off one target and is whipped across to strike a second in the same breath.

name: Folded Bellyswell
description: Rooted like a post with the club driven into the ground, the student holds firm under pushing.

name: Downward Clout
description: A flat blow delivered on a counted breath thumps the club into the chest like a mallet on a drum.

name: Downward Stout
description: The heavy end comes round from the side and pounds the soft flank beneath the ribs.

name: Raised Thickend
description: The shaft is tilted at a slope so a strike slides down it and past the student's body.

name: Burltrot
description: Three counted paces carry the student inside the opponent's reach without a wasted motion.

name: Girthpause
description: The butt end presses a weapon arm against the opponent's own body and holds it still.

name: Upward Cudgel
description: Two blows land one after the other, the first to open the guard and the second to hurt.

name: Planted Bulge
description: The weighted head hangs in front of the body and drags any incoming attack downward.

name: Thumpbump
description: The heavy head swings from low behind the hip up and across, carried by its own weight.

name: Hitching Wallop
description: The heavy head hooks behind the heel of a retreating foe and trips him backward.

name: Bulgelid
description: Leaning the haft into a swing from the side, the student stops it before it gathers speed.

name: Sharp Bludgeon
description: Sliding the hands down the shaft, the student drives the butt knob into the opponent's solar plexus.

name: Knobcowl
description: The short club is kept tight to the chest, guarding the face and ribs at grappling range.

name: Knob Drop
description: The butt of the hand club is jabbed straight out from the palm into the throat's base.

name: Fixing Cudgel
description: A tap behind the knee buckles the opponent's leg and drops his weight toward the ground.

name: Heartwood Lid
description: The club rolls along the forearm and bats a punch aside while the body turns out of line.

name: Cudgelpace
description: Pivoting on the lead heel, the student swings around an opponent's flank to a safer angle.

name: Gnawing Girth
description: Held like a hammer, the club chops down onto a raised forearm or the top of the foot.

name: Raised Roundhead
description: Hands set a forearm's length apart on the cudgel, the long bar covers head, chest and flank.

name: Bulgehit
description: A quarter turn of the hips drives the cudgel's head into the opponent's side with full weight.

name: Bulgeblow
description: Both hands stacked on the shaft, the cudgel's end is driven straight into the opponent's stomach.

name: Resting Burl
description: The cudgel is thrown flat across the body to catch a heavy downward cut on the wood.

name: Cloutamble
description: With the cudgel resting on the shoulder, the student closes ground in a light, hidden stride.

name: Hitching Belabor
description: The head hooks an arm, hauls it out of line and knocks the opponent's balance sideways.

name: Open Thump
description: Held high and let fall like a heavy bough, the cudgel's head crashes down onto the crown.
